conflicts.fact: Whether Gor Mahia win/draw/lose are equally likely (1/3 each) and what the sample space for a match is; also Lesson 1 asks whether a football match is an equally likely event
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 assigns P(Win)=P(Draw)=P(Lose)=1/3 and P(Win or Draw)=2/3 for a Gor Mahia match; Lesson 8 treats win probability differently (P=0.216 for three matches, i.e. 0.6 each) and Lesson 1/2 do not treat matches as equally likely.

conflicts.fact: Mutually exclusive event example in Lesson 8 is wrongly framed as a 'single draw from a shuffled pack' and both teams winning; also the definition of mutually exclusive events
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 defines mutually exclusive as cannot both occur on a single trial with P(A and B)=0 and uses Win vs Draw; Lesson 8 Scenario 3 asks about 'a single draw from a shuffled pack' with Gor Mahia and AFC Leopards both winning, mixing contexts.

conflicts.fact: Which coin is used in the coin-toss examples
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 uses a 10-shilling coin; Lesson 3 event card uses a flipped 20-shilling coin.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the cumulative model began and was last revised
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1-6 say the model began in Lesson 1; Lesson 7 says it was begun in Lesson 4 and revised in Lessons 5 and 6. Lesson 4 also says the model is retrieved from Lesson 3.

conflicts.fact: Multiplication rule and gambling claim: Lesson 7 says a betting stall at P(win)=1/3 over 180 spins pays out Ksh 1,800 while collecting Ksh 3,600 (inconsistent payout figures), and Lesson 7 uses a WIN-WIN coin/spinner probability of 0.5 per match vs Lesson 4's 1/3
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 models a Gor Mahia match as WIN 0.5/LOSE 0.5 (WIN-WIN ≈0.25); Lesson 4 gives P(Win)=1/3 for the same team's match; Lesson 8 uses 0.6 per match (0.216).

conflicts.fact: Length of Gor Mahia winning streak
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says 7 consecutive wins; Lessons 2 says 5 wins; Lessons 6 and 7 say 5 wins; Lesson 8 and others use 5 coin heads.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the evidence-gathering sequence
conflicts.versions: Lessons 2 and 6 call it an eight-lesson sequence, consistent with Lesson 8; Lesson 7 teacher says 'one lesson left', consistent; but Lesson 6 says first 'five lessons' built foundations including addition rule, consistent. No conflict beyond Lesson 3 overview referencing 'class coin-toss frequency table accumulated from Lessons 1-2' though Lesson 2 collected die/token data, not coin data.
